# Cell Biology Basics

The cell is the basic unit of life. Every living organism is made of one or more cells, and all cells come from pre-existing cells.

Cells are surrounded by a plasma membrane that controls what enters and leaves the cell. The membrane is made of a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins.

The nucleus stores the cell's genetic material in the form of DNA. During transcription, a gene's DNA sequence is copied into messenger RNA inside the nucleus.

Messenger RNA travels to the ribosomes in the cytoplasm. Ribosomes read the RNA code and assemble amino acids into a protein during translation.

Mitochondria produce most of the cell's usable energy as ATP through cellular respiration. Cellular respiration uses glucose and oxygen and releases carbon dioxide and water.

Plant cells also contain chloroplasts, where photosynthesis converts light energy, water and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen. Photosynthesis and cellular respiration are therefore linked.
